paragraphs.source_en:
‘And so it happens time and again, until the evil steed casts off his wantonness; humbled
in the end, he obeys the counsel of his driver, and when he sees the fair beloved is like
to die of fear. Wherefore at long last the soul of the lover follows after the beloved with
reverence and awe.’
 (Trans. R. Hackforth, in The Collected Dialogues of Plato, ed. Edith Hamilton and
Huntington Cairns (1961))
